behaviour: y_i = x_i / sqrt(mean(x_j^2) + 2^-16) in real units; with the Q8.8 scaling (value times 256) that is y_i = x_i * 1024 / sqrt(sum_j x_j^2 + 16), as a signed 16-bit number
Accuracy: |y_i - model_i| <= 1 LSB (1/256) for every lane; the all-zero input gives all zeros.
A write to GO clears READY and presents the loaded inputs for one clock; READY is 1 within 8 clocks and stays 1 until the next GO; OUT reads 0 while READY is 0.
LED[0] = READY, the other LEDs are 0.

"""Acceptance tests of c15_rmsnorm_unit against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from model import BUDGET_LSB, DESIGN_ID, GO, OUT0, STATUS, X0, bench_inputs, lanes_to_regs, rmsnorm_float


async def run_x(b: Board, x: list[int], what: str) -> None:
    for k, w in enumerate(lanes_to_regs(x)):
        await b.write(X0 + k, w)
    await b.write(GO, 1)
    await b.expect(STATUS, 1, f"READY {what}")
    y = []
    for k in range(8):
        w = await b.read(OUT0 + k)
        for h in (w & 0xFFFF, w >> 16):
            y.append(h - 65536 if h >= 32768 else h)
    ref = rmsnorm_float(x)
    err = max(abs(v - r) for v, r in zip(y, ref))
    assert err <= BUDGET_LSB, f"{what} input {x}: worst error {err:.3f} LSB above {BUDGET_LSB}; got {y}"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    assert await b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    for off in (X0, X0 + 7, STATUS, OUT0, OUT0 + 7):
        await b.expect(off, 0, f"reset value of {off:#x}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_special_vectors(dut):
    """All zero, one LSB, full scale both signs, alternating, a constant 5, a single -1."""
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    for k, x in enumerate(bench_inputs()[:7]):
        await run_x(b, x, f"special {k}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_single_large_input(dut):
    """One big number among fifteen zeros, at four lane positions."""
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    for k, x in enumerate(bench_inputs()[7:11]):
        await run_x(b, x, f"impulse {k}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_random_vectors(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    for k, x in enumerate(bench_inputs()[11:]):
        await run_x(b, x, f"random {k}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_registers(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    await run_x(b, bench_inputs()[12], "first")
    await b.write(X0 + 7, 0x12345678)
    await b.expect(X0 + 7, 0x12345678, "X7")
    await b.expect(STATUS, 1, "READY holds until the next GO")
    await b.write(OUT0, 0xFFFF)
    led = await peek(b.clk, dut.LED)
    assert led == 1, f"LED {led:04X}: only LED0 (READY) is lit"
    for off in (0x08, 0x12, 0x28, 0x7F):
        await b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped")
    await b.reset()
    await b.expect(STATUS, 0, "READY after reset")
    await b.expect(X0, 0, "X0 after reset")

spec_md:
# RMS norm unit behind the test shell

I want a block for the Nexys A7-100T's FPGA that rescales a vector of 16 numbers so that its root-mean-square value becomes 1 (the "RMS norm" a neural network applies before each layer), and I want to exercise it entirely from the test shell.

- The input is 16 numbers loaded over the shell, each a signed 16-bit number that is the real value times 256 (so 256 means 1.0), followed by a "go" command. The output is 16 numbers in the same format (real value times 256) that I read back
  over the shell, with a flag that says they are ready.
- Each output is the input divided by the square root of (the mean of the squares of the 16 inputs, plus a tiny constant 1/65536, in real units). The tiny constant makes an all-zero input give an all-zero output.
- Inputs range from a few units in the last place up to full scale, and the 16 numbers can have very different sizes (one big, fifteen zero). No floating-point blocks and no divider blocks; tables and multipliers
  are fine.
- Accuracy I need: every output within 1 unit of the last place (1/256) of the true value (rounded as you like).
- I will check the outputs for a few dozen input vectors against my own calculation with real numbers. CPU_RESETN clears the loaded inputs and the ready flag. LED0 shows the ready flag.
  The shell runs at 115200 baud on the USB-UART. The design ID is "RMSN".

Test hooks: top module `c15_rmsnorm_unit_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC, and the test shell's
`CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters as top-level parameters. There are no other time
constants.

what: A unit that rescales a vector of sixteen numbers so that their root-mean-square value becomes one. It squares and sums the inputs, finds the reciprocal square root without a divider or floating-point block, and multiplies each input by it. A tiny added constant makes an all-zero input give an all-zero output. Results must be within one unit of the last place.
where: Normalisation layers of this kind sit in front of nearly every layer of modern language models, so efficient hardware for them matters in inference accelerators.
